insight: Iraq's performance in the 2026 World Cup shows that hydration breaks have had a mixed impact on their gameplay. When they weren't pressing before a break, they tended to gain a slight advantage afterwards, with an average increase in momentum of +0.075 minutes per break, which suggests that these brief pauses allowed them to regroup and refocus. However, on the one occasion when Iraq was pressing before a hydration break, they actually lost momentum, with their average change in momentum dropping to -0.300 minutes per break, indicating that the pause may have disrupted their rhythm and intensity. Overall, Iraq seems to benefit from hydration breaks when they're not in an aggressive pressing mode, as it allows them to recharge and potentially gain an edge over their opponents.
